messages:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: elevated 5xx egress errors from region latam-sv1 (zone-b) — threshold breach at 3:12 UTC. Auto-escalation to oncall.

maria (oncall): Looking. Seeing lots of NAT timeouts and TCP RSTs from egress proxies in zone-b.

Ajay: Confirmed — 5xx rate ~12% over baseline for last 8m, connection errors spiking to 500s. Flow logs show burst of SYN_RECV backlog on nat-gw-b.

maria (oncall): Can we divert traffic away from latam-sv1:zone-b to latam-sv1:zone-a and us-east2 while we investigate?

SRE Lead - Keiko: Recommend immediate runbook step: reduce new allocations to zone-b, enable regional fallback routing. I'll coordinate with net-team to push route pref for peering to us-east2.

Ajay: Trying quick probe: 
```
curl -sS https://health-check.redwood-inference.internal/latam-sv1/egress -H 'X-Region: latam-sv1' || true
```
Responses show intermittent 502/504.

EmOps: Net-team standby. If we change outbound route preference for NAT we can relieve pressure but need to watch latency bump for APAC-adjacent customers. Any SLA-sensitive customers in this region?

Support - Emily: Pulling active customer list — two enterprise customers with dedicated capacity pinned to latam-sv1-zone-b (acct: ACCT-994, ACCT-111). Preparing customer drafts if we need to notify.

Juan R: I'll prepare the status page draft. Quick suggestion: be explicit about affected scope: "requests routed through zone-b experiencing elevated 5xx; mitigation in progress: traffic being diverted to zone-a and fallback regions".

maria (oncall): Taking mitigation step 1: disable autoscale add in zone-b to limit new work.

Incident Bot: Action logged: autoscale-policy latam-sv1-zone-b set to maintenance by maria at 3:21 UTC.

Ajay: Pushing short BGP preference change to edge-peers -> prefer us-east2 for outbound via peering-3. Net confirmed they can push in ~3m.

SRE Lead - Keiko: When net flips preference, add a temporary routing policy in runtime to avoid quantized model shard placements in zone-b. That prevents hot-shard re-creation.

Product - Lina: Draft for status page (suggested language):
"We are investigating elevated 5xx errors affecting outbound egress from latam-sv1 zone-b. We are diverting new traffic to adjacent zones and fallback regions while we remediate. Customers using dedicated capacity pinned to zone-b may see increased latency or transient failures; we will update when we have more details."

Support - Emily: Customer draft ready:
"Hi — we are aware of elevated errors from latam-sv1 (zone-b) impacting outbound requests. Our engineers are diverting traffic and are working on a fix. If you are on dedicated capacity pinned to zone-b, our team will reach out directly with mitigation options. We apologize for the disruption and will follow up with timeline estimates."

Juan R: Status-per-region quick table for status page (internal):
- latam-sv1:zone-b — degraded (egress 5xx high) — mitigation: traffic diversion in progress
- latam-sv1:zone-a — healthy — accepting diverted traffic
- us-east2 — healthy — receiving fallback traffic
- eu-west1 — unaffected

Ajay: Net rolled preference at 3:26 UTC. Early metrics: 30% of flows now rerouted to us-east2, zone-b 5xx rate starting to drop (from 12% -> 6% in last 5m). Latency for rerouted flows +45–80ms median.

maria (oncall): Will monitor for error drop to <1% before re-enabling scale. Keep dedicated customers engaged — Emily, can you confirm outreach for ACCT-994 and ACCT-111?

Support - Emily: Reached out to ACCT-994 via urgent channel; they request ETA and prefer a phone call. ACCT-111 asked for mitigation logs, sending now.

SRE Lead - Keiko: Next troubleshooting: inspect nat-gw-b kernel conntrack and CPU; if conntrack exhausted, flush with care. Ajay — can you check conntrack size and SYN backlog?

Ajay: Conntrack entries at 96% of quota on nat-gw-b, SYN backlog high. Kernel CPU elevated on gateway instance. Suspect NAT process exhaustion due to sudden traffic pattern.

maria (oncall): Decide: keep diversion live, open a low-impact conntrack soft-clear (see runbook) and scale up a replacement nat-gw in zone-b as restoration step.

Incident Bot: Runbook step executed: conntrack soft-clear initiated on nat-gw-b by Ajay at 3:33 UTC. Scaling request to infra for replacement nat-gw instance submitted.

EmOps: Infra started new nat-gw instance in zone-b; will attach to egress pool in ~4m.

Ajay: After conntrack clear, 5xx dropped to 2.3% but still above baseline. New nat-gw pending attach.

maria (oncall): Good. Prepare final customer note: include timeline, what we did, and next steps. Juan, finalize status page and note 'service impact mitigated, active monitoring'.

Juan R: Status page updated: "Mitigation in progress — egress errors reduced; diversion active; dedicated customers contacted. Monitoring for full recovery."

Support - Emily: Sent updated message to ACCT-994 and ACCT-111 with mitigation steps and expected follow-up in 30m.

SRE Lead - Keiko: Handoff: maria, please summarize current state and any open actions for next oncall.

maria (oncall): Summary for handoff:
- Current: egress 5xx reduced to ~1.2% after diversion + conntrack clear; latency increased for rerouted flows (~+50ms).
- Open actions: attach new nat-gw in zone-b and verify stability; validate conntrack behavior under typical load; re-enable autoscale for zone-b after 30m of stable metrics.
- Customer comms: Emily has notified affected enterprise customers; product & comms to send public status update (done).

SRE Lead - Keiko: Thanks. I will remain on call for 2 more checks. Maria — handoff to Ajay at 04:10 UTC for next shift; leave notes in runbook. :thumbsup:

Ajay: Acknowledged. I'll pick up monitoring and watch for reattach logs.

Incident Bot: Incident state: mitigation in progress -> partial-service-restored. Timeline logged.

maria (oncall): Closing the urgent page for this shift, leaving postmortem checklist in /incidents/latam-sv1-zone-b-recon.md.

Support - Emily: If anyone needs the customer templates used, I put them in #support-drafts.

Product - Lina: Thanks team. Suggest a short post-incident retrospective next week to discuss NAT sizing and fallback routing policy.

SRE Lead - Keiko: Agreed. We'll schedule a 30-minute blameless postmortem.

Ajay: Monitoring graphs look stable for now. Marking thread for follow-up. :white_check_mark:
